_doc: The ONE read-only policy shared by the Go agent and the Python control plane (#682, #691).
agent/go embeds this file; src/homepilot/adapters/readonly_policy.json must be a byte-identical copy
(tests/test_readonly_policy.py and agent/go/readonly_policy_test.go both fail on any drift).
Commands are POSITIVE-ONLY: a command is allowed only if its whole text matches its pattern.
Patterns use the syntax shared by Go RE2 and Python re, carry no anchors, and are matched against
the WHOLE command (Go wraps them in ^(?:...)$, Python uses fullmatch).
read_tier=false keeps a command out of the MCP read tier (exec_on_guest_readonly) while the agent
still accepts it from an admin caller. path_checked=true routes the argument through read_paths,
read_paths is DEFAULT-DENY: a path must be in allow_exact or under allow_prefixes (or a write prefix),
and must not hit any deny rule. Deny rules always win, including over an operator's

ps._doc: No BSD 'e' anywhere: 'ps e' / 'ps auxe' print every process's environment. A dashed cluster may start with -e (all processes) and otherwise holds only letters that are valid UNIX options, so procps never falls back to reading it as BSD letters (where 'e' would mean environment).

ip._doc: Read verbs only (show/list/get). No set/add/del/flush/change/replace, no -batch, no netns exec.

ss._doc: No -K (kill sockets), -D (dump to a file), -F (read a filter file), -N (netns), -E (never returns), and no long options. Filter words cannot start with '-'.

systemctl._doc: No daemon-reload: it is a state change and stays a privileged-only command.

journalctl._doc: Read flags only. No --flush/--rotate/--vacuum-*/--sync/--relinquish-var/--setup-keys/--update-catalog/-D/--file, no -f (never returns). Option values never start with '--', so a value slot cannot smuggle a flag.

cat._doc: One absolute path, checked against read_paths exactly as read_file checks it.

docker._doc: Agent-side safe set only: kept out of the MCP read tier (docker inspect prints container environments).
